title: Labor-Replacing Automation and Finance
near_miss_reason: Every reported column that uses the binary robot-deployment indicator (rdeploy2_lag0, = 1 from the firm's first robot year onward) includes the same 14 time-varying firm controls ($controls: log assets, log age, cash, tangibility, sales, tax, selling-expense, labor-intensity ratios, wage per employee, new-product ratio, R&D, subsidy, ROA, productivity). No column reports the binary indicator with firm and year FE alone. The companion columns use continuous robot capital (rpstock2 = robot stock/assets, rpstock4 = robot stock/employees), and Table 5 is IV.
eligible_reason: The design qualifies in principle: rdeploy2_YYYY = 1 if robotyear <= YYYY (Data processing.do lines 425-436), an absorbing firm-level binary treatment that switches on at firm-specific first-deployment years, estimated with firm and year FE on a 2015-2017 CEGS firm panel (4,569 firm-years) with never-treated firms. But all columns add time-varying controls, so the paper is a near-miss rather than eligible. The data are also not in the package: the CEGS survey is restricted and the Dropbox link in the README offers only synthetic versions of the proprietary datasets.
design_notes: Panel: Chinese manufacturing firms from the China Employer-Employee Survey (CEGS), years 2015-2017, firmid x year (Table 3_step 1/2 construction in SAS). Treatment variants: rdeploy2_lag0 (binary deployment), rpstock2_lag0 (robot stock / total assets, continuous), rpstock4_lag0 (robot stock / employees, continuous); all winsorized at 0.5/99.5 where continuous. Outcomes: lever (total debt / assets) and irate (interest expense / debt, only for fsample==1). Table 3 (Table 3_step 3_regression.do line 50): reghdfe y xvar_lag0 $controls, absorb(firmid year) noconstant, no vce option (reghdfe default SEs). Table 4 (Table 4_step 2_regression.do line 52): same regression on didsample==1, a 'staggered' subsample built in Table 4_step 1_construction.sas from province-industry pairs whose robot-subsidy policies started in 2016 or 2017 (pharmaceuticals Hubei 2016; cement Guangdong 2016; special equipment Hubei 2016 and Sichuan 2017; automobiles Sichuan 2016 and Jiangsu 2017), dropping adopting firms in other provinces of the same industries. Table 5: ivreghdfe lever/irate on rpstock (continuous) instrumented with tpi and IFR-based robot stocks, absorb(province year). Table 7: listed-firm sample, absorb(stkcd year). Table 8: interactions with log variables. Tables 9-10: splits by heterogeneity indicators (paravar / mvar_high) and interactions with xvar. Figure 1 / Tables 1-2: SAS descriptives.
estimators_reported: twfe_static_with_controls (binary deployment indicator, firm + year FE)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Within the 2015-2017 panel the switchers are firms with first robot year 2016 or 2017 (two cohorts); firms with robotyear <= 2015 (or robot purchases already in 2015) are always-treated; firms without robots are never-treated. The didsample policy shocks are also dated 2016 or 2017.

specs.exclusion_reason: 14 time-varying firm controls in the only reported column; near-miss
specs.treatment_definition: 1 if the firm's first robot deployment year (robotyear, CEGS d5_r13) <= current year, or if robotyear is missing and the firm reports robot purchases in or before the current year (Data processing.do 425-436); 0 otherwise
specs.controls: at_log age_log liqratio tanratio saleratio taxratio xslratio labratio salary npratio rdxratio tsubratio roa prod (time-varying)
specs.data_file: E:/Datasets contructed/BASELINE_REG.dta (NOT shipped; synthetic version on authors' Dropbox)
specs.reported_location: Table 3, leverage panel, Robot Deployment column (table3x1)
specs.notes: Continuous rpstock2 / rpstock4 columns follow in the same loop.

specs.outcome: irate (interest rate = financial expense / debt, winsorized)

specs.treatment_definition: as above, on the staggered policy subsample
specs.sample_condition: didsample == 1 (province-industry pairs with robot-subsidy policies from 2016 or 2017; see Table 4_step 1_construction.sas lines 38-59)
specs.reported_location: Table 4, leverage panel (table4x1); interest-rate panel at line 64 with fsample==1
specs.notes: The authors label this the DID / staggered sample.

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying controls; subgroup splits and xvar interactions
specs.treatment_var: xvar_lag0 (rdeploy2 / rpstock2 / rpstock4) by paravar==0/1 and c.paravar#c.xvar_lag0
specs.notes: Table 5 is IV (ivreghdfe, absorb(province year)); Table 7 uses listed firms (absorb(stkcd year)); Table 8 uses log interactions.

data_files_note: The local package contains only code (SAS and Stata), logs and the README. 0Readme.docx states that the CEGS survey data are 'only accessible by authorized users' and that a Dropbox link provides 'synthetic versions of proprietary datasets (with the same number of observations, same variable names, and same variable distributions as the original ones)'. IFR robot data and CSMAR data are licensed.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, ivreghdfe, winsor2, outreg2) for all regressions; SAS for data construction, descriptives (Tables 1-2) and Figure 1.
priority_note: Near-miss (controls in every column); no real data in the package (synthetic only via external link).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Binary treatment construction verified in Data processing.do lines 425-436 and Table 3_step 1_construction.sas line 113 (rename rdeploy2 -> rdeploy2_lag0). The panel has only three years (2015-2017), so even a controls-free re-estimation would rest on two switching cohorts and many always-treated firms.
